utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, registrar. Today we are the 14th of May, 2007. I'd like to welcome the representatives from the Prosecution, Defence counsel, and the accused. Without forgetting, of course, all staff members who are giving us a helping hand. As you know, the Appeals Chamber has handed down as a decision whereby it rejected the application made by the Prosecution which challenged the decision we had handed down on time limitations. The Prosecution, therefore, has 293 hours, as the registrar prepared a chart last week on the time already used. According to my calculations, the Prosecution would have 86 hours left to finish the presentation of its case. Why is this the case? Well, 293 minus 207, which they have had already, equals 86 hours. That said, Mr. Mundis, I have looked at the chart you prepared providing a witness names. Some witnesses have been withdrawn, some are on standby, and some had been scheduled. It is now for you for the remaining witnesses to use these 86 hours as best as possible. That said, Mr. Mundis, as far as I'm concerned, you may resort to 92 ter Rule for a number of your witnesses. Of course, given that a number of witnesses have already testified about those facts, this would enable you to put a few questions using -- by using a number of documents, and this would enable Defence counsel to conduct their cross-examination. Rule 92 ter allows for time restriction and, therefore, you might not have to use all of the time for the witnesses you have prepared. I have looked at your chart, and I realised that you withdrew a number of witnesses from your list, witnesses which the Trial Chamber may find useful. If you have decided to withdraw these witnesses, the Trial Chamber feels it is entitled to call these witnesses to testify if they feel it is necessary. So basically you have 86 hours left to finish the presentation of your case. You now have the floor, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, counsel, and everyone in and around the courtroom. I can assure the Trial Chamber that the Prosecution team is continuing to evaluate all of the numbers and particularly the issue of witness scheduling, and we will take into consideration, obviously, the comments made by the Presiding Judge. While I'm on my feet, if I could, I just wanted to also convey two other issues concerning scheduling, and for that if I could briefly go into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The next issue, Mr. President, concerns the schedule for the month of June. The Prosecution has been operating under the procedure of the Chamber whereby we disclose or distribute the calendar on the 15th of the month preceding that for which the schedule covers. I would ask in this instance that the June schedule not -- that we be allowed to distribute the June schedule no later than Friday the 18th, that is to Friday, rather than tomorrow, and I say that because there are a couple of witnesses that are still slightly unsettled, and if I were to distribute the calendar tomorrow it's extremely likely that on Friday I would have to distribute a revised schedule. So we would ask that instead of disclosing or distributing it tomorrow, that we be given until Friday, and perhaps we can -- we can do it on Thursday, but Friday to be on the safe side, and that will cover the schedule through the month of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. The Trial Chamber grants your request, and you may give us your schedule at the latest on Friday. There are two witnesses that have been scheduled for this week. We shall bring in the first witness in a few moments. Given the time allocated to the latter, the Prosecution will have four hours for this witness, and Defence teams will have five hours to cross-examine this witness. So, that said, Mr. Prlic's Defence will have one hour; Mr. Pusic, Defence counsel, will have one hour; Mr. Coric's Defence counsel will have one hour. The three other accused will each have 40 minutes each. You can, of course, allocate the time according to your needs. You have five hours all in all. So if there are no delays, the Prosecution should be able to finish today, with a bit of luck should be able to finish his examination-in-chief, which means that we would start with the cross-examination tomorrow morning through to Wednesday. And for the remaining time we could start on the examination-in-chief of the next witness and perhaps even start the cross-examination of this witness. Given that there has been one hour allocated for the examination-in-chief of the second witness and one hour allocated to Defence teams for the cross-examination of the said witness. Mr. Praljak's Defence counsel might just decide to cross-examine this witness, given the position the second witness is. That said, last week we handed down our written decision relating to the way in which the witnesses should be examined. This decision was recorded on Friday and will be translated into English. And for the accused who do not understand English, I would like to mention the fact that we had decided, on the one hand, to recall the Rules 85(B). Let me -- 85(B), 90(F), and 90(H). According to Rule 85(B), the Judges are entitled to put any question to the witness at any time of the examination. In the decision we handed down, we have clearly indicated that we shall consider the guidelines which were presented by both parties on the 22nd of March, 2007. In other words, the rule, we will only put questions to the witness once each party will have concluded its examination-in-chief or cross-examination respectively, unless, of course, we come up exceptional circumstances, in which case we can only take the floor immediately. As you know, over the last few weeks we have applied this particular procedure. In addition, when handing down this will decision we also stipulated that as far as questions put by an accused are concerned, we reminded everyone of the guidelines (C) of our revised decision of the 28th of April, 2006, and we specified that an accused who wishes to put a question must be permitted to do so. And because, or in the event of exceptional circumstances, the accused may put questions, but the former needs to explain why it is he wishes to put that kind of question to the witness, either because these are questions of a technical nature in which the accused is particularly well-versed, particularly when it has to do with military matters, or because the witness mentions the accused's name particularly, either because he's met him or because he knows him, and in that case the accused may be asked questions directly by -- the witness may be asked questions directly by the accused. So all of this should run smoothly without anybody being prejudiced. The accused should be entitled to put their questions also, under those particular conditions which I have mentioned and which are primarily of a technical nature. Now, there's a legal matter I would like to address and which relates to the nature of the questions put when a topic was not addressed during examination-in-chief. We have felt that when that situation arises, the question -- when the question has not been raised or is not part of the scope of the examination-in-chief, in that case the accused who wishes to put questions during the cross-examination must formulate his question in the most neutral manner possible, and the question must not be leading in that case. So must for the gist of our decision which will be translated very shortly, I believe, but we have already applied this decision. As you know, the upcoming witness has been granted protective measures, so I will ask to move into private session [as interpreted]. The private session has been agreed upon pursuant to our order. Could we please draw the blinds therefore. Could we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours. Several parties have submitted lists of documents to be tendered through Witness Grant Finlayson. The list submitted by the OTP shall be given Exhibit number IC 553. The list submitted by 2D shall be given Exhibit number IC 554. The Exhibit list submitted by 3D shall be given Exhibit number IC 555. And the list submitted by 4D shall be given Exhibit number IC 556. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you, registrar. Let's move back into private session now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 15th day of May, 2007, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 6.55 p.m.,
